Custom Order Policy

Custom Order Policy

What a bubble mailer order commits both sides to: where changes can be made, what we put right, what sits with you, free US shipping, and how to report a problem.

Contact UsView Products

Made-to-order supply is not retail, and applying retail expectations to it causes most of the disputes in this industry. A printed run produced to your artwork cannot be restocked, resold or returned to a shelf, because there is no shelf it belongs on. This page sets out what that means in practice: what can be changed and at what point, what happens if an order is wrong, what shipping costs, and what a run of bubble mailers genuinely commits both sides to.

Where changes can be made, and where they cannot

An order passes through points after which a change costs a run rather than an email.

  • Before the quotation is confirmed. Anything can change: size, finish, print, quantity. This is the point to be undecided.
  • After confirmation, before the proof. Specification changes are still possible. The quotation is reissued so what is agreed stays unambiguous.
  • At proof stage. Artwork changes belong here. Ask for as many rounds as you need; a proof round costs far less than a reprint.
  • After proof approval. Production is scheduled against the approved proof. Changes from this point mean a new proof and, once material is committed, a new run.
  • After production. Custom printed mailers cannot be resold to anyone else. Changes at this point mean a fresh order.

What we are responsible for

If any of these happens, tell us and we will resolve it.

  • The order does not match the approved proof. Wrong color, wrong placement, wrong artwork. The proof is the reference and we are held to it.
  • The order does not match the written specification. Wrong size, wrong finish, wrong closure, wrong quantity band.
  • A manufacturing defect. Failed seals, adhesive that does not release cleanly, split seams or print defects across the run.
  • A short delivery. Counts are verified by carton before dispatch, and a genuine shortfall is ours to make good.
  • Damage in transit. We arrange every shipment, so report transit damage promptly with photographs of the cartons as they arrived.

What sits with you

These are the things we cannot check on your behalf, and they are why the proof and sample stages matter.

  • Errors in artwork you approved. A misspelled word, an old web address or a wrong handle on an approved proof cannot be caught by us, because we have no way to know what it should say.
  • Choosing a size that turns out not to fit. This is why samples exist. A sample before a run costs almost nothing; a run in the wrong size costs the run.
  • Ordering more than you can use. Particularly on seasonal work. We will quote a contingency quantity separately so you can see what it costs.
  • Rights in the artwork you supply. Confirming you may reproduce it commercially is your responsibility.

Returns

Because every order is supplied against a written specification, we do not accept change-of-mind returns on plain or printed stock. Where an order does not match the approved proof or the written specification, is short, or has a manufacturing defect, we make it right by replacement or credit at our cost. That commitment is the return policy, and it applies to every order shipped within the United States.

Shipping

Shipping is free to any address in the United States, for a single case or a full pallet, plain or printed. The price on your quotation is the delivered price. Pallet-quantity programs can be released on a schedule at no extra shipping cost, so you are not storing a full pallet at once.

Quantity variation on a manufactured run

Production runs do not stop at an exact unit, so a manufactured order may deliver slightly above or slightly below the quantity ordered. This is normal in the industry rather than a defect. The tolerance that applies to your order is stated on your quotation, along with how any variation is charged. If an exact quantity matters, a set number of units for a subscription drop for instance, say so when you ask for the quote so we can specify accordingly.

Reporting a problem

Contact us as soon as you find an issue, with the order reference, photographs of the cartons and the affected mailers as received, and the approximate proportion of the delivery affected. Keep the affected stock until the matter is resolved, because we may need to see it. The fastest route is the address and number on the contact page, and we confirm next steps in writing so both sides have a record.

Questions about the custom order policy

Plain stock is supplied against a written specification too, so change-of-mind returns are not accepted. If the size, finish or count is not what was specified, or the mailers are defective, we replace or credit them.
